forwardMergeFingerprint.procedure: skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md, The unchanged-diff check, run with base main and the fileset ~(.legion | docs/solutions)
forwardMergeFingerprint.soWhat: A full test round, not the bare gates. The branch's own lines moved: sjawhar/legion#2528 (clusterOnly) merged at 9d60d92f and conflicted in gcp/dispatch.go, gcp/dispatch_kube.go and infra/README.md, and the resolution carries a change of its own — three rows added to dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals and to its test table — which is new behaviour this branch had not had before and which no round of mine had tested.

workspaceRecreated: This turn began with a recreated workspace. I re-read the record and the branch rather than my memory: retro had already run (4fd1344e added four docs/solutions learnings, b87d1fbf removed .legion/INFRA-550/), the merger had completed once (cb96806b), and the issue then came back to implementing for the forward merge. My round-1 and round-2 test handoffs are therefore not in the tree; they are in history at 02b24ffbf923 and b8fa955eb2a7, and this file is written afresh. Nothing of mine was lost: both rounds were pushed before they completed.

implementerProof.how: Both of round 3's entries re-run independently at this head. The module: `go test ./gcp/ -count=1` with the two mkfs.ext4 tests skipped is `ok ... 81.770s`, so the merged tree's own suite holds, TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly among it. The consumer surface: I built the plugin again from this head at a version of my own (0.0.4), read its schema with the real Pulumi CLI v3.268.0, generated the SDK with `pulumi package add` and wrote my own consumer program, not the implementer's. Every observation they recorded came back — the three inputs still plain and none required, requiredInputs now region and hostname alone, the SDK fields *bool/*int/*int, the providers gate on a valid row, and the clusterOnly refusal of natsInCluster. I drove more than they did: all three new refusal rows rather than one, the explicitly-false case, the precedence against the bounds check, and the accepted control (clusterOnly with none of the three).

proof.criterion: The merge's own new behaviour: clusterOnly refuses each of this branch's three inputs by name (the three rows added to dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals, implement.json round 3).
proof.surface: The built pulumi-resource-envoy-infra driven by the real Pulumi CLI v3.268.0 on a file:// backend under $TMPDIR with PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN empty — the consumer surface agent-infra's dispatch/ program uses, not the unit test.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && go build -ldflags '-X main.version=0.0.4' -o $TMPDIR/infra-550-test3/pulumi-resource-envoy-infra ./cmd/pulumi-resource-envoy-infra; pulumi plugin install resource envoy-infra 0.0.4 --file <binary>; pulumi package add <binary>; go build ./...; then `pulumi preview --stack proof --non-interactive` once per row, each row's inputs from PROOF_CLUSTER_ONLY / PROOF_IN_CLUSTER / PROOF_NATS_REPLICAS / PROOF_STREAM_MAX_BYTES
proof.observed: Each of the three is refused by its own name: `envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch tester-dispatch: natsInCluster configures Dispatch, which clusterOnly does not build: unset it, or unset clusterOnly`, and the same sentence for natsReplicas and for streamMaxBytes. natsInCluster set explicitly false is refused too, which is right and is what every other pointer input of the census does (the row tests `!= nil`, not the value). With all three set the refusal names natsInCluster, the first of the three in DispatchArgs' own order. The clusterOnly refusal also comes before the bounds check: clusterOnly with natsReplicas 6 is refused as a Dispatch input rather than as an out-of-range one, which is the right order, since under clusterOnly the number configures nothing.
proof.negativeControl: clusterOnly set and none of the three reaches `envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch needs a "gcp" provider in its providers option`, the providers.Require gate — so the three refusals are the inputs being named and not clusterOnly refusing everything. The non-clusterOnly rows accept all three, which is the other half of the same control.

proof.criterion: A consumer can still pass the three inputs after the merge, on the surface agent-infra's dispatch/ program uses (plan acceptance table, row 5), re-proved at the merge head as a forward merge requires.
proof.surface: The same plugin and CLI, through the Go SDK the CLI generates from the plugin's own schema at this head.
proof.command: pulumi package get-schema <binary>; then the valid and refusing preview rows above
proof.observed: The schema still carries natsInCluster {"type":"boolean","plain":true}, natsReplicas and streamMaxBytes {"type":"integer","plain":true}, beside #2528's clusterOnly, and requiredInputs is now `region` and `hostname` alone — #2528's breaking change, not this branch's. The generated SDK declares NatsInCluster *bool, NatsReplicas *int and StreamMaxBytes *int on gcp.DispatchArgs (sdks/sjawhar-envoy-infra/envoyinfra/gcp/dispatch.go:88-102). Both valid rows — natsInCluster true with natsReplicas 5 and streamMaxBytes 1, the two bounds, and the SOCKS5 mode with neither number — reach the providers.Require gate, which only an accepted resolve reaches. My consumer program needed pulumi.StringRef on the inputs #2528 made optional, which is that change's own cost and not this branch's.
proof.negativeControl: Four refusals at the resolver, each naming its own input and each arriving before the provider gate: `natsReplicas 6 is above 5, the most copies NATS keeps`, `natsReplicas 0 is below 1; leave it unset for one copy`, and `streamMaxBytes 0 is below 1; leave it unset for no limit` (the same for -1).

proof.criterion: With an in-cluster address set, neither container carries a SOCKS5 setting and both carry the address and the numbers; each number is left unset unless given; the SOCKS5 mode is untouched (plan acceptance table, rows 1, 2 and 3) — all of it re-driven, because the merge restructured gcp/dispatch_kube.go (#2528 removed the dispatchKubernetes struct and changed the function's returns).
proof.surface: The rendered pod templates and the registration census of the three Deployments, through the gcp package's Pulumi mock engine.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && go test ./gcp/ -count=1 -skip 'TestTheDataDiskIsFormattedOnlyWhenItReadsAsZerosToItsEnd|TestARefusedDataDiskIsNeverFormattedOnALaterBoot'; and a throwaway probe file of my own (gcp/zz_tester_probe3_test.go, deleted before this handoff) run with go test ./gcp/ -run TestProbe3 -v
proof.observed: The package is `ok` (81.770 s), every golden comparison included — #2528's new gcp/testdata/dispatch-registrations.golden among them, which this branch does not change and which the pull request's file list confirms is untouched. My probes: every spelling of a local server is still refused under natsInCluster (nats://[::1]:4222, nats://localhost:4222, nats://LOCALHOST.:4222, nats://127.42.7.9:4222 and the scheme-less localhost:4222, not only 127.0.0.1); both numbers render at both bounds (5 and 1) on both containers with no ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY key; the ordered environments are unchanged from round 2 — envoy-dispatch [HOME … NATS_URLS ENVOY_ALLOW_REMOTE_NATS NATS_NKEY_SEED_FILE ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES ENVOY_URL ENVOY_TOKEN] and envoy-listener [PORT ENVOY_LISTEN_HOST ENVOY_MACHINE_ID NATS_URLS ENVOY_ALLOW_REMOTE_NATS ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES NATS_NKEY_SEED_FILE ENVOY_API_TOKEN]. The registration census is exact: the default mode registers 39 resources and the in-cluster mode 38, and the one absent is `kubernetes:core/v1:Service::example-dispatch-tailnet` — nothing else dropped, nothing new appeared, which is the check the merge's restructure of that file most needed.
proof.negativeControl: natsInCluster set explicitly false, which no committed test passes: both containers carry ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY=example-dispatch-tailnet.dispatch.svc.cluster.local:1055, the front door's NetworkPolicy admits example-dispatch and example-dispatch-listener on 1055, and both Deployments depend on the front door's Deployment and its Service. So the in-cluster assertions pass on the mode, not on keys missing from every rendering after the merge.

proof.criterion: Production, before the change: the baseline the production check after the merge compares against (plan T8, surface 3). It proves nothing about this change.
proof.surface: The production dispatch namespace of the cluster this pod runs in.
proof.command: kubectl -n dispatch get pods -o json, filtered to the NATS variables of each container
proof.observed: Unchanged from round 2: envoy-dispatch and envoy-listener each carry NATS_URLS, ENVOY_ALLOW_REMOTE_NATS, ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY and NATS_NKEY_SEED_FILE, with neither ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS nor ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES, and the front door's tailscale container carries TS_SOCKS5_SERVER. Pod names move between rounds (the app pod is dispatch-64f94c99cc-q8vk4 now, and was dispatch-57688ffbc9-twn97 when the implementer first recorded it), so the production check should match on the Deployment.
proof.negativeControl: The read is of the live pods rather than of a rendering: a wrong namespace or container name returns no row at all, and every expected row was present with the SOCKS5 variable set, which is the state the production check must find changed.

observations.what: O1 and O2 of rounds 1 and 2 stand unchanged and are already settled: natsInCluster and natsUrl must change in one apply, with natsUrl set to the in-cluster Service name, and the apply runs only after INFRA-551's bridge policy admits namespace dispatch, reading both rollouts complete and the app's /healthz reporting NATS connected.
observations.evidence: Round 1 measured both from this pod: the hub's tailnet MagicDNS name does not resolve from an ordinary cluster pod while envoy-hub.envoy.svc.cluster.local does, and the app's readiness reads only Postgres while the listener exits on a failed initial connect.
observations.judgement: INFRA-14's architect took both on 2026-10-29 and put them in INFRA-553's spec version 23. The code stays as it is. Nothing for this pull request.

observations.what: Worth one line for the reviewer rather than a finding: under clusterOnly, natsInCluster set explicitly to false is refused, because the census row tests whether the input was set at all. That is the shape every other pointer input of dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals has (existingNamespace, replicas, pprofPort and the rest), so it is the convention rather than a quirk of these three.
observations.evidence: gcp/dispatch.go:585-587 — `{"natsInCluster", args.NatsInCluster != nil}` — and the preview row `clusterOnly + natsInCluster FALSE (explicitly set)` above, refused by name.
observations.judgement: Consistent with #2528's own design and with the learning this pull request writes down (docs/solutions/infra/an-optional-mode-that-zeroes-an-input-inherits-every-refusal-that-input-carried-pr2529.md). No change asked for.
